description: Interactive step-based progressive comparison for Grade 7 Mathematics — Mean vs Median patterns. Redesigned with Singularity Design System. Two-column comparison table with indigo (#4A4DC9) header for Mean and orange (#FF7212) header for Median. Rows appear one at a time with slide-in animation. Each row shows a scenario name on the left, with the mean value in indigo and median value in orange. Row 1: balanced newspaper data with mean ≈ median shown with an approximately-equal sign between them. Row 2: Poovizhi's family with a downward red arrow on the mean side showing it pulled below median. Row 3: bookworm data with an upward red arrow on the mean side showing it pulled above median. Row 4: pattern summary with visual arrows. Row 5: formal definition of central tendency with icons. Each row highlighted on reveal with a soft glow. Mini dot plots beside each row showing data points, mean marker (indigo), and median marker (orange). Poppins font throughout. Singularity 5-colour palette: indigo (#4A4DC9), orange (#FF7212), gradient purple-to-orange (#533086 to #FC9145), white background (#FFFFFF), dark text (#2D2D3F). Mobile-responsive table that scrolls horizontally on narrow screens. Practice mode shows correct answer highlighted in green when user picks wrong.
topic: Statistics — Mean vs Median Patterns and Measures of Central Tendency
curriculum: NCERT Ganita Prakash Grade 7 Part-II Chapter 5 — Connecting the Dots

learn.description: Progressive step-by-step comparison: reveals three scenarios one at a time, then pattern summary, then central tendency definition. Rows animate in with slideInFromRight. Active row gets a soft indigo glow. Teaching notes appear at bottom for each scenario.

practice.description: Students predict whether mean will be greater than, less than, or equal to median based on data characteristics. Three pill-shaped answer buttons. On wrong answer: selected button highlights red, correct button highlights green with checkmark icon and bounceIn animation. Feedback banner shows correct answer in a green pill. Practice state resets automatically via useEffect when navigating between questions.

real_world.description: Real-world examples showing when mean or median is more appropriate. Each example shows a large icon, description, and side-by-side Mean vs Median cards with slide-in animations.

teaching_notes.step_1_balanced: Point out that mean and median are close — this is the 'normal' case when data has no extreme outliers.
teaching_notes.step_2_low_outlier: Ask: 'Which direction did the outlier pull the mean?' The low outlier (118 cm) drags the mean below the median.
teaching_notes.step_3_high_outlier: Ask the student to PREDICT the relationship before revealing. The high outlier (40 stories) pulls mean above median.
teaching_notes.step_4_pattern: Let the student state the pattern in their own words first before showing the summary cards.
teaching_notes.step_5_central_tendency: Introduce the formal term 'measures of central tendency' and explain two different ways of finding the centre.

instructions_for_student: Watch as three different data sets appear one by one. For each, compare the mean and median. After seeing all three, look for the pattern: when is the mean pulled below the median? When is it pulled above? Think about WHY this happens before the explanation appears.

behavior.practice_state_reset: useEffect watches currentStepIndex and selectedMode. Whenever either changes (via Next, Previous, progress dots, or mode switch), practiceAnswer and showFeedback are both reset to null/false automatically.
behavior.wrong_answer_feedback: When user selects a wrong answer: (1) selected button turns red with red border, (2) correct answer button highlights green with green border, checkmark icon, and bounceIn animation, (3) feedback banner shows 'Not quite!' in red plus a green pill showing the correct answer label.
behavior.correct_answer_feedback: When user selects the correct answer: selected button turns green, feedback banner shows '🎉 Correct! You understand the pattern!'
behavior.row_reveal: Each scenario row is revealed via slideInFromRight animation when the corresponding learn step is reached. Rows persist once revealed so the comparison table builds progressively.
